questions.solution:
Doubtful points : $-1, 0, 1, \sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3}, 2$
at $x = \sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3}$
$f(x) = \left(2x^{2} + x - [x]\right) + \left[x^{2}\right] =$ Discount (first bracket: Cont., second bracket: Cont.)
at $x = -1$ :
RHL $\Rightarrow f(x) = (2 - 1 - (-1)) + 0 = 2$
$f(-1) = 2 - 1 - (-1) + 1 = 3$ } Dis.

Let the mean and the standard deviation of the probability distribution
X | $\alpha$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-3$
P(X) | $\frac{1}{3}$ | K | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$
be $\mu$ and $\sigma$, respectively. If $\sigma - \mu = 2$, then $\sigma + \mu$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{3} + k + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{4} = 1$ $\quad \Rightarrow k = \frac{1}{4}$
$\mu = \frac{\alpha}{3} + \frac{1}{4} - \frac{3}{4}$
$\mu = \frac{\alpha}{3} - \frac{1}{2}$
$\sigma = \sqrt{\left(\alpha^{2}\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + 9\frac{1}{4}\right) - \left(\frac{\alpha}{3} - \frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}}$
$\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{2\alpha^{2}}{9} + \frac{\alpha}{3} + \frac{9}{4}}$
$\sigma = \mu + 2$
$\sigma^{2} = (\mu + 2)^{2} \Rightarrow \frac{2\alpha^{2}}{9} + \frac{\alpha}{3} + \frac{9}{4} = \frac{\alpha^{2}}{9} + \frac{9}{4} + \alpha$
$\frac{\alpha^{2}}{9} - \frac{2\alpha}{3} = 0$
$\alpha = 0$, (reject) or $\alpha = 6$
($\because$ $x = 0$ is already given)
$\Rightarrow \sigma + \mu = 2\mu + 2$
$= 5$

If
$1 + \frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3}} + \frac{5 - 2\sqrt{6}}{18} + \frac{9\sqrt{3} - 11\sqrt{2}}{36\sqrt{3}} + \frac{49 - 20\sqrt{6}}{180} + \ldots$
upto $\infty = 2\left(\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}} + 1\right)\log_{e}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, then $11a + 18b$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$S = 1 + \frac{x}{2\sqrt{3}} + \frac{x^{2}}{18} + \frac{x^{3}}{36\sqrt{3}} + \frac{x^{4}}{180} + \ldots\infty$
Put $\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} = t$, where $x = \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}$
$S = 1 + \frac{t}{2} + \frac{t^{2}}{6} + \frac{t^{3}}{12} + \frac{t^{4}}{20} + \ldots$
$S = 1 + t\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) + t^{2}\left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + t^{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4}\right) + t^{4}\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{5}\right)$
$S = \left(1 + t + \frac{t^{2}}{2} + \frac{t^{3}}{3} + \frac{t^{3}}{4} + \ldots\right) - \left(\frac{t}{2} + \frac{t^{2}}{3} + \frac{t^{3}}{4} + \frac{t^{4}}{5} + \ldots\right)$
$S = \left(t + \frac{t^{2}}{2} + \ldots\right) - \frac{1}{t}\left(t + \frac{t^{2}}{2} + \frac{t^{3}}{3} + \ldots\right) + 2$
$S = 2 + \left(1 - \frac{1}{t}\right)(-\log(1 - t)) = \left(\frac{1}{t} - 1\right)\log(1 - t) + 2$
$S = 2 + \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}} - 1\right)\log\left(1 - \frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$
$S = 2 + \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}\right)\log_{e}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}$
$S = 2 + \frac{\left(\sqrt{6} + 2\right)}{2}\log_{e}\frac{2}{3} = 2 + \left(\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} + 1\right)\log_{e}\frac{2}{3}$
$a = 2, b = 3$
$11a + 18b = 11 \times 2 + 18 \times 3 = 76$

questions.stem:
Let $a > 0$ be a root of the equation $2x^{2} + x - 2 = 0$.
If $\lim_{x \to \frac{1}{a}} \frac{16\left(1 - \cos\left(2 + x - 2x^{2}\right)\right)}{\left(1 - ax^{2}\right)} = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{17}$, where $\alpha, \beta \in Z$ then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$2x^{2} + x - 2 = 0$ with roots $a$, $b$
$2x^{2} - x - 2 = 0$ with roots $\frac{1}{a}$, $\frac{1}{b}$
$\lim_{x \to \frac{1}{a}} 16 \cdot \frac{\left(1 - \cos 2\left(x - \frac{1}{a}\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{b}\right)\right)}{4\left(x - \frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}} \times \frac{4\left(x - \frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}}{a^{2}\left(x - \frac{1}{a}\right)^{2}}$
$= 16 \times \frac{2}{a^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{a} - \frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}$
$= \frac{32}{a^{2}}\left(\frac{17}{4}\right) = \frac{17 \cdot 8}{a^{2}} = \frac{17 \times 8 \times 16}{\left(-1 + \sqrt{117}\right)^{2}}$
$= \frac{136 \cdot 16}{18 \cdot 2\sqrt{7}} \times \frac{18 + 2\sqrt{7}}{18 + 2\sqrt{7}}$
$= \frac{136}{256}\left(18 + 2\sqrt{7}\right) \cdot 16$
$= 153 + 17\sqrt{17} = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{17}$
$\alpha + \beta = 153 + 17 = 170$

questions.stem: If $f(t) = \int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{2x\,dx}{1 - \cos^{2}t\sin^{2}x}$, $0 < t < \pi$, then the value of $\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\frac{\pi^{2}dt}{f(t)}$ equals _____.
questions.solution:
$f(t) = \int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{2x}{1 - \cos^{2}t\sin^{2}x}dx$ .....(1)
$= 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{(\pi - x)dx}{1 - \cos^{2}t\sin^{2}x}$ ....(2)
$2f(t) = 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{\pi}{1 - \cos^{2}t\sin^{2}x}dx$
$f(t) = \int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{\pi}{1 - \cos^{2}t\sin^{2}x}dx$
divide & by $\cos^{2}x$
$f(t) = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{\sec^{2}x\,dx}{\sec^{2}x - \cos^{2}t\tan^{2}x}$
$f(t) = 2\pi\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\frac{\sec^{2}x\,dx}{\sec^{2}x - \cos^{2}t\tan^{2}x}$
$\tan x = z$
$\sec^{2}x\,dx = dz$
$f(t) = 2\pi\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{dz}{1 + \sin^{2}t \cdot z^{2}}$
$= \frac{\pi^{2}}{\sin t}$
Then $\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\frac{\pi^{2}}{f(t)}dt$
$= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin t\,dt$
$= 1$
